title: 950 cars, 1,000 spaces. How far do the last cars go? Roll forward 81 spots per car, random retry 12.
description:
950 cars into 1,000 spaces. How far do the last cars go? One row of 1,000 spaces, drawn as 50 columns by 20 rows (space 999 wraps to space 0). 950 cars arrive one at a time; each car wants one preferred spot drawn uniformly from the seeded generator, and the same preferred spots feed both lots. Top lot, roll forward: a blocked car drives forward one space at a time to the next free spot (linear probing). Bottom lot, fresh random spot: a blocked car draws a new random spot from a second seeded stream and tries there until it finds a free one (random probing; a retry may hit the same taken spot twice). A car's spots passed is the number of taken spots it drove past or tried before it parked (probes minus one). Seed 0, two streams spawned from one SeedSequence. Time-lapse: the first 900 cars in 17 seconds, the last 50 slower.

Measured:
- cars 901 to 950 (the lot 90 to 95 percent full): roll forward 80.9 spots passed per car on average (closed form 98.0), max 360 (car 943), median 41; fresh random spot 12.4 per car (closed form 12.8), max 122, median 6; ratio 6.5; rounded to 81 and 12 on the card
- closed forms: linear probing expects (1 + 1/(1 - a)^2) / 2 probes to insert at load a, 50.5 at 0.90 and 200.5 at 0.95; random probing expects 1 / (1 - a) tries, 10 at 0.90 and 20 at 0.95; spots passed = probes minus one, so 49.5 and 199.5 against 9 and 19; averaged over cars 901 to 950 (loads 0.900 to 0.949): 98.0 against 12.8
- blocks of fifty cars, average spots passed (roll forward / fresh random spot): cars 551-600 2.6 / 1.3, 601-650 4.4 / 1.8, 651-700 5.4 / 2.4, 701-750 7.1 / 2.4, 751-800 6.8 / 3.8, 801-850 19.9 / 4.3, 851-900 37.1 / 7.4, 901-950 80.9 / 12.4 (closed forms 2.3 / 1.4, 3.1 / 1.7, 4.2 / 2.1, 6.1 / 2.6, 9.5 / 3.5, 16.1 / 4.7, 32.6 / 7.1, 98.0 / 12.8); under 1.5 in both lots up to car 550
- longest run of consecutive taken spots: 265 against 39 at 900 cars, 515 against 72 at 950 cars; the roll-forward lot's first run over 100 forms after car 824 and its first run over 200 after car 846
- all 950 cars: roll forward 8,551 spots passed in total (9.00 per car), 503 cars parked at their preferred spot, the first car past 100 spots is car 839; fresh random spot 2,063 in total (2.17 per car), 493 cars at their preferred spot
- the last car (car 950, preferred spot 609) is an unlucky draw in the wrong direction: with roll forward it drove past 2 spots (609 to 611); with a fresh random spot it tried 122 taken spots before it parked at 682, a 0.95^122 = 0.2 percent event at that load. That is why the payoff is the average over the last fifty cars, and the single-car readout stays on screen as it is
- checks, seeds 1 to 5, cars 901 to 950 average (roll forward / fresh random spot): 57.7 / 13.9, 31.9 / 10.3, 49.0 / 16.1, 56.3 / 7.9, 42.1 / 12.7; longest run at 950 cars 495 / 102, 177 / 55, 298 / 88, 392 / 134, 437 / 91
- check, a 100,000-space lot with 96,000 cars at seed 0: cars at load 0.895 to 0.905 pass 48.3 / 9.23 spots on average (closed forms 49.6 / 9.01), cars at load 0.945 to 0.955 pass 222.1 / 19.35 (closed forms 201.5 / 19.07), cars 90,001 to 95,000 pass 99.2 / 13.07 (closed forms 99.5 / 12.86); longest run 984 / 94 at 90 percent full and 2,579 / 148 at 95 percent

Why: with roll forward, a blocked car parks at the end of the run it landed in, so the run grows by one, and when two runs meet they merge into one. A longer run catches more preferred spots, so it grows faster still. That is why the taken spots clump and the late cars drive past hundreds of spots: linear probing's (1 + 1/(1 - a)^2) / 2 blows up as the lot fills. A fresh random spot has no memory of where the runs are: every retry succeeds with the same chance, the share of free spots, so the tries are a geometric count with mean 1 / (1 - a), and the taken spots stay evenly dotted. Hash tables that use linear probing have exactly this problem at high load, which is why they are resized long before they are full.

Rerun sims/parking/parking.py with projects/parking/manifest.json and you get these numbers exactly.
